dedupe_keys.name: rapid estimation of housing non recovery after the 2015 nepal earthquake

description: This study by Sabine Loos and co-authors, published in Communications Earth and Environment in February 2023, develops a data-driven way to estimate non-recovery, meaning areas with the potential to fall behind during recovery, soon after a disaster instead of relying on building damage alone. It demonstrates the approach for housing reconstruction after the 2015 Gorkha earthquake in Nepal, relating survey data on reconstruction progress collected five years after the event to predictors that would be available in most countries, such as population from WorldPop, remoteness from the World Bank, forest cover, topographic slope from SRTM and shaking intensity, to identify ongoing social and environmental vulnerabilities associated with non-recovery. The combined and scaled predictor data and the R code used to build the model are deposited on Zenodo (release v1.0.0, February 2021). Coverage: earthquake-affected districts of Nepal. Access: open access article and Zenodo repository. Licence: article CC BY 4.0; the Zenodo release is CC BY-NC 4.0. Caveats: recovery is measured only as housing reconstruction, and the survey data themselves are not redistributed in full. Simulation uses: an example of recovery-aware prioritisation that can complement damage-based post-disaster models. Related records: the StEER reconnaissance data and the HUD CDBG-DR disaster recovery grants.
